clue.text: Doctor's run, gone dubiously to hide money in France?

indicators.note: to hide means the anagram wraps round and conceals the money
done dubiously, the letters of run and gone are put in a doubtful new order

parts.note: the euro is the currency of France, here in the plural

explanation.surface: A doctor seems to be running a shady scheme to stash cash in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Doctor's' stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay; 'dubiously' marks the anagram and 'to hide' the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain surgeon is a medical specialist, so is a kind of doctor.

clue.text: No way alcohol is remedy

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
rum is a spirit, an alcohol

explanation.surface: A teetotaller's slogan: refusing drink is the cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack medicine, a supposed cure-all, so a remedy of sorts.

clue.text: Annoying lump wanting leader to form coalition

indicators.note: wanting leader means the first letter is lost

parts.note: a bunion is a painful, annoying swelling on the foot

explanation.surface: A painful lump, losing its head, somehow forms an alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a joining of parties or states, as is a coalition.

clue.text: Birds love good person with lots of bread

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
ST, saint, is a crossword good person
bread is slang for money, so lots of it is riches

explanation.surface: Birds adore a kindly soul with plenty of bread to share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' means money here, not food for the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostriches are large flightless birds of Africa.

clue.text: Take back hunting hound, no good at all

indicators.note: no good at all says every G, for good, is removed, not just one

parts.note: a gundog is a dog used in shooting and hunting

explanation.surface: Someone wants to return a hunting dog that proved useless.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Gs go from GUNDOG because of 'at all'.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo something is to reverse or retract it, to take it back.

clue.text: Suspect rogue spy stays on campsite

definitions.note: the definition is plural like the answer; stays are supporting ropes

indicators.note: suspect, as an adjective, says the letters are not to be trusted as they stand

explanation.surface: A dubious secret agent is staying at a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stays' looks like a verb about lodging; it is the noun for supporting lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines pegged out to hold a tent upright are stays, the supports of a campsite.

clue.text: Characters regularly in vogue turned unconventional

indicators.note: characters regularly takes every second letter of the following words

explanation.surface: Fashion has swung to the eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré is a borrowed French word for bizarre or beyond the bounds of convention.

clue.text: Fancied playing European opposition

indicators.note: playing means the letters of fancied are put into play in a new order

explanation.surface: A fancied European team is playing the opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is open resistance, a stance of opposition.

clue.text: The Parisian with fever a distance at sea

parts.note: le is French for the, as said in Paris
ague is an old word for a shivering fever

explanation.surface: A Frenchman, feverish, finds himself far out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is an old measure of about three miles, used for distances at sea.

clue.text: In unnatural manner — as long-legged entertainer walks?

definitions.meaning: stiffly and awkwardly, as forced prose
a circus performer on stilts moves as if stilted, read literally

explanation.surface: Awkward walking compared with a stilt-walker at a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilted speech is stiff and artificial, so done that way is unnaturally; a stilt-walker literally goes on stilts.

clue.text: Matter requiring most of London police

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is cut away

parts.note: the Met is the Metropolitan Police of London

explanation.surface: Something needs the attention of Scotland Yard.
explanation.walkthrough: THE MET, London's Metropolitan Police, loses its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: The matter of a talk or essay is its subject or theme.

clue.text: Current individual reflected in middle of mirror is artist

indicators.note: in places the reversed pair inside the central letters
middle of takes the two central letters of mirror
reflected suits a mirror: the pair is read backwards

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A painter sees himself reflected in a looking-glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns I ONE into ENOI, which sits between the two Rs at the centre of MIRROR.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: Call on man for shelter

indicators.note: on means the call comes after the man in an across answer

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man or chap
to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: Visit a fellow to ask for a roof over your head.
explanation.walkthrough: COVE is dated British slang for a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A covering, such as a roof or canopy, gives shelter.

clue.text: Soggy batter rejected and withdrawn

indicators.note: rejected, thrown back, means the word is turned round

parts.note: to batter is to ram, as with a battering ram
a withdrawn person is shy and retiring

explanation.surface: A batsman, soggy and rejected, retreats into himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshy ground is boggy and waterlogged, so soggy.

clue.text: Row with Heather is vexing

parts.note: a rank is a row, as of soldiers or taxis
ling is the common heather plant

explanation.surface: A quarrel with someone called Heather is annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name; it is the moorland plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rankling keeps irritating, so it is vexing.

clue.text: Tea I need to prepare for confined person

indicators.note: to prepare means these letters are made up afresh in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone in custody needs tea made for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A detainee is held in custody, a person kept confined.

clue.text: Excitedly glance over unlimited baked food

indicators.note: over means the anagram sits above the next piece in a down answer
excitedly means the letters of glance are jumbled up
unlimited means without its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly eyes something fresh from the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excitedly' marks the anagram, 'unlimited' strips the ends from the bake word, and 'over' places the jumble above it, as this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel cake is a light sponge, an item of food.

clue.text: With time in force, start to rumble fraud

indicators.note: in means the time letter goes inside the word for force

parts.note: to impose is to force something on someone

indicators.note: start to takes the opening letter of rumble

explanation.surface: A con artist rumbled with time running out.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposter is someone pretending to be another, a fraud.

clue.text: Nice-looking cab carrying daughter east

indicators.note: carrying means the cab holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: a hansom is a two-wheeled horse-drawn cab

explanation.surface: An attractive cab takes a girl eastwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome describes good looks, so attractive or nice-looking.

clue.text: Bears almost killed badger

parts.note: bears means has, as a tree has or bears fruit

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: slew is the past tense of slay, killed

explanation.surface: Bears nearly killed a badger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badger' is the verb, to pester, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester or harass them.

clue.text: Sparkling silver accompanying cooked meal

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of meal are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A meal served with gleaming silverware.
explanation.definitionFit: Agleam means glowing or gleaming, so sparkling.

clue.text: A group of soldiers in pristine tower

indicators.note: in means the pair goes inside the word for pristine

parts.note: in mint condition means pristine
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of soldiers

explanation.surface: A troop of soldiers is posted in an immaculate tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque.

clue.text: Roughing up lout is no answer

indicators.note: roughing up means the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Beating up a thug solves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A solution is the answer to a problem or puzzle.

clue.text: Discussions with head of science to replace learner's assignments

indicators.note: to replace says one letter stands where another was

parts.note: talks are discussions
L is the learner driver's plate letter

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of science

explanation.surface: Talks led by a science teacher replace a pupil's homework.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are jobs set for someone, assignments.

clue.text: Part of wheat surplus sent away from borders

parts.note: a glut is an excess, a surplus

indicators.note: away from borders means the outer letters are stripped off

explanation.surface: Excess grain is shipped off from the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluten is a protein present in wheat, so it is part of the grain.

clue.text: Your old mate heaving at aromatic plant

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your

indicators.note: heaving, throwing out, means the letters of at are removed

explanation.surface: An old friend retching beside a fragrant herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a fragrant herb, an aromatic plant used in cooking.

clue.text: Warning! Cockney's in north

parts.note: in means at home, which a Cockney says without the h

explanation.surface: A shout of alarm from a Londoner up north.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney, from London's East End, drops the h, so home becomes 'OME.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign of things to come, a warning.

clue.text: Joins course for sportspeople

definitions.meaning: a seaside golf course for players

explanation.surface: Someone signs up at a sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To link things is to join them; a links is a golf course on coastal land.

clue.text: Adventurous boy from Surrey was motivated to return

indicators.note: to return says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A daring lad from an English county is driven to come home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' marks the letters held within 'Surrey was motivated'; 'to return' reads them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain's Tom Sawyer is the classic adventurous boy of American fiction.

clue.text: Soldiers on mountains in test about alienation

indicators.note: in means those pieces go inside the jumbled test
about means the letters of test are turned around into another order
on means the soldiers come after the mountains in an across answer

parts.note: a range is a chain of mountains
men are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops in the hills undergoing a trial drift apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges TEST as EST...T, and RANGE then MEN go 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Estrangement is the state of being cut off from others, alienation.
